result:
The test DB is gitignored, so only the intended files changed. Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (4 tests, 0 fail) pass.

`PostController.update()` (app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88) was hand-building its redirect as a raw `new Response(null, { status: 302, ... })`, and a 302 makes the browser replay the original method — so the PUT to `/posts/<id>` was re-sent as another PUT, which redirected again, hence `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS` and the form never advancing (the row was already written, which is why a manual reload showed the edit). `store()` and `destroy()` were unaffected because they use the framework's `this.redirect()`, which answers non-GET requests with 303 See Other. I replaced the hand-built response with `this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)` plus a short comment explaining why the status matters, matching the other actions; validation still short-circuits before the redirect, so error rendering on the edit form is untouched. I also added tests/PostUpdate.test.ts, which migrates the test database, creates an author and post, and asserts that a successful `PUT /posts/:id` answers 303 with `Location: /posts/<id>` and persists the new title, while an empty payload still comes back 422.
